name: Julius
overview: Julius is a male figure identified as a centurion of the Augustan cohort, a Roman military unit, as noted in Acts 27:1. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are provided in Scripture. His role as a centurion places him within the Roman military structure during the early Christian era.
namesAndTitles: The name Julius appears once in Scripture and does not have a specific meaning or divine attribution noted. It is presented simply as a proper name in Acts 27:1 without additional significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Julius beyond his military position as a centurion. No relatives or personal connections are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Julius holds significance as a Roman centurion who interacts with the early Christian narrative during Paul's journey, illustrating the intersection of Roman authority and the spread of the Gospel. His presence in Acts 27:1 highlights the providential protection and guidance over Paul as he travels under Roman custody. Julius's role contributes to the unfolding of God's plan in the New Testament by facilitating Paul's mission despite the challenges of imprisonment.
